The Department is requesting the purchase of eight new Motorola APX500 radios each of the next two fiscal
years to increase officer safety, reliability, and internal and external communication. The existing Motorola
mobile radios are currently over 15 years old and are no longer supported by Motorola for parts or software.
Our radio service provider advises there is no way to put future software updates on these radios, which may
make them inoperable in the next 18-24 months, Interagency Communications Interoperability (ICI), is in the
process of upgrading their infrastructure, which also requires the City to upgrade equipment software. The
departments current radios are UHF and 700 band frequency radios. When ICI goes from phase one to phase
two of their infrastructure upgrade frequencies will split, requiring a software upgrade to our current radios.
The City's radio service provider does not believe the current radios will support this new software. In
addition, LA County's communication center, Los Angeles Regional Interoperable Communications System
(LARICS), is making changes to their infrastructure that will also require a software upgrade in order to have
channels available for mutual aid. Having the ability to communicate with surrounding agencies, the airship, and
agencies within the City'sCal OES mutual aid area is critical for operations.

  Request Description and Justification
(Provide a description of your request that includes a justification describing the benefit of the expenditure to the department/City)
The Police Department is requesting body worn cameras for its officers to increase officer safety, decrease liability to
the City, increase evidence collection, and management by capturing video evidence. Overall, this request will help
further the City Council's Continued Public Safety Excellence Priority Initiative. The Police Department currently only
has in-car video, which collects limited video evidence. It does not capture video evidence when the officer is not
directly in front or inside of the vehicle, or inside a residence, which is where most contacts occur. This new body worn
camera system will include a body worn camera for each officer and cadet, to be used when interacting with the public,
new in-car video for each patrol vehicle, unlimited Cloud storage, unlimited Cloud storage for the drone program,
redaction software to assist Records with Public Records Act requests, and video evidence requests by the District
Attorneys Office.

The estimated cost includes body worn cameras, all new in-car cameras, 5 year warranty with free replacement of body
worn cameras after 30 months, redaction software for the Records Manager for PRA requests, unlimited Cloud
storage, and training. The first year includes installation cost and training. This request is eligible to be paid for by
COPS funds.

In FY 18-19, the City Council approved a biennial program to replace small engine equipment such as

The Department owns several dozen small engine tools under 50 hp used for trimming, blowing, trenching,

transitioning its small engine tools to electric. This transition will provide the added benefit of noise and
pollution reduction as gas-powered equipment is phased out.

The Department owns five riding mowers for maintenance activities involving mowing the 35 acres of Lacy
Park, as well as the landscaped medians on Huntington Drive and Sierra Madre Boulevard. Two of the mowers
are electric-powered (purchased in FY 23-24), with the remaining three being gas-powered. A new electric
mower will help improve the frequency of the City's maintenance activities at Lacy Park as well as medians and
other landscaped areas of the public right-of-way. Additionally, the purchase of an electric mower will help the
City meet new State requirements regarding the usage of electric vehicles and equipment. Beginning in 2024,
manufacturers will begin phasing out gas-powered mowers, making it more difficult to find replacement parts
for the City's existing equipment. The Department recommends purchasing a mower every other year
beginning until the mower fleet is completely electric. As this is an electric mower, AQMD funds may be used
to assist with the purchase. The estimated price based on quotes obtained from qualified vendors is $60,000,
although this amount may be able to cover the purchase of two mowers depending on potential AQMD
exchange rebates. Staff will explore potential funding opportunities to lessen the overall financial impact to the
City. A new mower has an expected useful life of 20 years, and would improve maintenance staff efficiency.

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department completes a monthly report for the Public
Safety Commission, providing an overview of department activities, significant
incidents, and monthly statistics.

DISCUSSION

Personnel
Probationary Firefighter/Paramedic Jake Martinez began his regular shift
rotation on February 25, 2024. The Fire Department recently extended
conditional offer letters to two additional candidates for the position of
firefighter/paramedic. The department anticipates to reach full staffing by the
end of March.

Inspections
The Fire Department began annual business inspections during the first week
of March for properties located in the City’s commercial districts. Annual
inspections are required for all commercial properties, school properties, and
the Huntington Library to ensure compliance with fire and life safety codes.
There are 233 commercial properties within San Marino as well as 23
properties identified by the department as target hazards.

  PAGE 46 of 66
 San Marino Fire Department personnel, including Chief Rueda, recently
conducted a walkthrough of the solar installation at the San Marino
Community Church. Fire inspections are required for all solar installations to
ensure compliance with California Fire Code and San Marino Municipal Code.

Significant Incidents
On March 3, at approximately 2 AM, Engine 91 and BC9 responded to a
commercial structure fire in Pasadena. Pasadena Fire Department arrived
onscene and initiated fire attack and ventilation. Upon E91 and BC9 arrival, it
was clear that the visible smoke did not indicate any structure or content
involved in fire. Upon investigation, it was determined that the property owner
had built a security deterrent that would activate a smoke machine in the
ceiling when the burglar alarm was activated. Following the incident, San
Marino Fire Department personnel conducted refresher training on size-up
protocols and how to read smoke.

On March 5, 2024 San Marino Police and Fire Departments were alerted by a
resident to a disturbance at the Chase Bank adjacent to the City Hall campus.
San Marino firefighters observed and extinguished a small fire on the signage
at the Chase Bank. San Marino police officers detained a male suspect who
was in the area – the individual confessed to the crime and was subsequently
arrested for arson by the San Marino Fire Department. The individual was on
parole for a previous arson offense and is a registered arsonist.

Training
San Marino Fire and Police personnel participated in cross-training to
familiarize both departments with each others equipment and vehicles. Fire
Department personnel learned about Police gear and patrol cars, and how to
remove PD ballistic gear in the event of an injury needing immediate care.
Fire personnel gave a demonstration on how to use the ambulance gurney,
medical gear locations, and the drag rescue device on each firefighter’s
turnout gear.

Community
On Friday, March Fire Department personnel participated in the Carver
Elementary 2024 Jog-a-Thon. Later that day, San Marino firefighters visited
San Marino Girl Scout Troop 6341 to assist the scouts in earning their First
Aid badge. Firefighters demonstrated how to administer CPR and First Aid,
including how to treat injuries, burns, fractures. The scouts were then able to
practice their skills using the departments first aid and CPR training aids.
